item.content:encoded: El FMI dijo el jueves que la economía mundial había capeado la crisis provocada por la guerra en Oriente Medio mejor de lo que se temía y que aún se esperaba que la producción económica mundial crezca alrededor de un 3% en 2026, pero advirtió de que los riesgos eran altos. Julie Kozack, portavoz del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI), señaló que los precios del petróleo y el gas seguían siendo altos y que la crisis energética derivada de la guerra aún no había terminado. Las presiones de la deuda mundial también iban en aumento y el proceso de desinflación tras la crisis del costo de la vida de 2022 se había estancado. Las expectativas inflacionistas mundiales han aumentado, pero siguen bien ancladas en el largo plazo, dijo Kozack en una rueda de prensa habitual del FMI. "Hasta ahora, a pesar de seis meses de guerra en Oriente Medio, la economía mundial ha demostrado su resiliencia", señaló Kozack, y añadió que el uso de las reservas de petróleo y gas había permitido a algunos países hacer frente a las crisis energéticas provocadas por la guerra. "Seguimos en camino de alcanzar un crecimiento mundial de alrededor del 3%, pero la incertidumbre, como venimos diciendo desde hace bastante tiempo, sigue siendo alta", señaló. En julio, el FMI había bajado ligeramente su previsión de crecimiento mundial para 2026 a un modesto 3,0%, frente a un promedio del 3,5% previsto para 2024 y 2025.

item.title: Bolsonaro, Lula statistically tied in simulated Brazil runoff, Atlas/Bloomberg poll shows
item.description: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva are statistically tied in a simulated runoff ahead of next month's election, an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll showed on Thursday, with the right-wing lawmaker now holding a narrow numerical edge over the leftist incumbent.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva are statistically tied in a simulated runoff ahead of next month's election, an AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll showed on Thursday, with the right-wing lawmaker now holding a narrow numerical edge over the leftist incumbent. The eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro would receive 46.4% of the vote in a second-round runoff, compared with 46.2% for Lula, the poll showed. In late August, Lula led the senator 47.1% to 42.6%. In a first-round scenario, Lula is seen leading with 43.0% of the vote, followed by Bolsonaro (37.4%), Augusto Cury (6.6%) and Renan Santos (6.5%). The previous poll [USN:L6N44S0LF TEXT:"showed Lula"] at 43.4% and Bolsonaro at 33.7% in the first round. If no candidate wins more than 50% of valid votes in the October 4 first round, the two frontrunners advance to a runoff on October 25. AtlasIntel surveyed 5,000 people between September 4 and 9. The poll has a margin of error of 1 percentage point.

item.title: India's NSE cuts IPO size by over 15%, to launch next week
item.description: The National Stock Exchange of India has cut the size of its long-awaited IPO by more than 15% and will take investor orders next week, its prospectus showed on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The National Stock Exchange of India has cut the size of its long-awaited IPO by more than 15% and will take investor orders next week, its prospectus showed on Thursday. The offering, expected to be one of India's largest, comes after years of delays and at a time when India's IPO market regains momentum, paving the way for a fresh wave of marquee listings, including billionaire Mukesh Ambani's [USN:L4N44P0TT TEXT:"Jio"]. NSE's IPO will be an offer for sale with no fresh capital raised, where existing investors including State Bank of India (SBI.NS) , Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and General Insurance Corporation of India (GENA.NS) will offload 126.4 million shares, down from the 148.91 million planned earlier, with SBI selling the most shares. NSE's share sale will open for subscription on September 17 and close on September 21, with anchor investor bidding scheduled for September 16, the bourse said in a filing. Shares will likely be priced between 1,700 rupees and 1,785 rupees apiece, Reuters [USN:L6N4500Z8 TEXT:"reported"] on Wednesday. NSE, the country's biggest exchange by trading volumes, dominates the derivatives market and has benefited from a surge in retail trading in the world's most populous country. NSE's revenue from operations stood at 166 billion rupees ($1.74 billion) for the year ended March, with a profit of 103.02 billion rupees. The bourse had 129.09 million registered investors and 2,978 listed entities. ($1 = 95.4400 Indian rupees)

item.title: An opioid appeal test limits of judicial power in mass torts
item.description: After nearly a decade of litigation and $50 billion in settlements, the nationwide opioid litigation brought by local and state governments finally seemed to be winding down. Then the Ohio federal judge overseeing it allowed hundreds of plaintiffs this summer to add two deep-pocketed defendants to their cases.
item.dc:creator: Jenna Greene
item.content:encoded: After nearly a decade of litigation and $50 billion in settlements, the nationwide opioid litigation brought by local and state governments finally seemed to be winding down. Then the Ohio federal judge overseeing it allowed hundreds of plaintiffs this summer to add two deep-pocketed defendants to their cases. The judge's move has prompted an urgent appeal by the companies, pharmacy benefit managers Optum Rx and Express Scrips, which argue that the judge made a procedural error by allowing the parties to amend their complaints en masse years after the deadline to do so had passed. The companies, which deny wrongdoing, argue that U.S. District Judge Dan Aaron Polster should have evaluated the requests of all 800 plaintiffs — ranging from small rural towns like Cherokee, Alabama, to major American cities including Detroit and Cleveland — individually. The appeal now before the Cincinnati-based 6th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals highlights a central tension in multidistrict litigation: How much leeway should judges have to deviate from the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure when managing the massive proceedings? If the appeals court finds the judge overstepped, it likely doesn’t mean Optum and Express Scripts would escape the litigation altogether. But it could force plaintiffs to clear additional hurdles before adding the companies to their cases, slowing the litigation and potentially easing settlement pressure on the defendants. The procedural dispute comes after many of the opioid litigation's largest players, including drugmakers, distributors and pharmacy chains, agreed to [USN:L1N3SJ0KO TEXT:"settlements"] over their alleged roles in a crisis that has killed more than 800,000 people since 1999. The pharmacy benefit managers, however, remain in the MDL along with some retail pharmacies and generic drugmakers. The plaintiffs allege that Optum and Express Scripts, which process claims for insurance coverage of prescription medications, colluded with drugmakers to promote opioids, oversupplying communities with addictive medications. A spokesperson for Optum, which is owned by UnitedHealth Group and generated $ 154.7 billion in revenue in 2025, said in a statement that the company “did not contribute to this crisis, and on the contrary has been a leader in fighting opioid abuse.” Express Scripts, which was [USN:KCN1OJ2DM TEXT:"bought by Cigna"] for $54 billion in 2018 and no longer releases stand-alone revenue, declined comment. A spokesperson for the plaintiffs’ legal team, which includes lawyers from Motley Rice; Simmons Hanly Conroy; Farrell & Fuller and Spangenberg, Shibley & Liber, declined to comment. In the early days of the opioid litigation, which began in 2017, pharmacy benefit managers were named as defendants in fewer than 100 lawsuits. Polster in court papers later described the companies' business practices as "unusually opaque," which may have made them a less-obvious initial target. In 2024, plaintiffs’ lawyers asked Polster for permission to amend hundreds of complaints to add Optum and Express Scripts as defendants. In part, they pointed to "key information" produced in litigation brought by Jefferson County, Missouri, that they said shed new light on the role of the companies in the opioid crisis. But their request came five years after Polster’s March 16, 2019, deadline for most litigants to make such changes. This is where the Rules of Federal Civil Procedure come into play. Rule 15 says judges should allow parties to amend their lawsuits “when justice so requires.” And Rule 16 says changes are permitted if plaintiffs can demonstrate a “good cause” for their failure to comply with the original schedule. Defense lawyers from Sullivan & Cromwell; Alston & Bird and Quinn, Emanuel, Urquhart & Sullivan argue that Polster erred by allowing the plaintiffs to add their clients without first conducting a case-by-case analysis. In a court order, the judge said it would require “colossal resources” to look at each case individually, and that doing so would not serve the efficiency goals of an MDL. Instead, he issued a series of rulings addressing common issues, ultimately allowing the 800 amended complaints. Defense lawyers counter that federal rules don’t allow such a shortcut, and that the judge was required to consider if each plaintiff individually satisfied Rule 15 and Rule 16. Many do not, they argue. For example, they say the plaintiffs and their lawyers had access to the relevant documents about pharmacy benefit managers as early as July 2018, but failed to act on the information. They also note that in 2020, the Sixth Circuit reversed Polster for a similar procedural move in the opioid MDL, rebuking him for allowing two Ohio counties to add untimely claims. “MDLs are not some kind of judicial border country, where the rules are few and the law rarely makes an appearance,” the panel held . The MDL court “must find efficiencies within the Civil Rules, rather than in violation of them.” Now defense lawyers want the Sixth Circuit again to determine whether Polster crossed the line, and to reinforce its earlier warning that the rules of civil procedure offer no exception for multidistrict litigation. The procedural question prompted a trio of amicus briefs last week in support of the pharmacy benefit managers. The U.S. Chamber of Commerce in its brief warned of potentially “devastating” effects on American businesses and the national economy if MDL judges aren't required to follow the same procedural rules that govern other civil cases. The Chamber also noted that MDLs now account for nearly two-thirds of all private civil litigation at the federal level, writing that they are “the predominant means for suing businesses in federal court today.” Mandamus petitions – where a litigant asks an appeals court to intervene before a case reaches final judgment – are rarely granted. But the pharmacy benefit managers’ protest appears to have piqued the Sixth Circuit’s interest. The appellate court ordered plaintiffs' lawyers, and "invited" Polster, to respond by Sept. 15.

item.title: Democrata dos EUA pede medidas contra motoristas que cochilam ao volante de carros da Tesla
item.description: Um deputado democrata pediu, nesta quinta-feira, que uma agência de segurança automotiva dos Estados Unidos tome medidas sobre o uso indevido dos sistemas Autopilot e Full Self-Driving da Tesla, citando dezenas de vídeos que parecem mostrar motoristas dormindo ou distraídos ao volante.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: Um deputado democrata pediu, nesta quinta-feira, que uma agência de segurança automotiva dos Estados Unidos tome medidas sobre o uso indevido dos sistemas Autopilot e Full Self-Driving da Tesla, citando dezenas de vídeos que parecem mostrar motoristas dormindo ou distraídos ao volante. Em uma carta ao secretário de Transportes dos EUA, Sean Duffy, o deputado Raja Krishnamoorthi, de Illinois, citou uma reportagem da NBC News que identificou 43 vídeos que parecem mostrar pessoas dormindo no banco do motorista de carros da Tesla em movimento, 17 neste ano. Krishnamoorthi afirmou que a Administração Nacional de Segurança Rodoviária (NHTSA, na sigla em inglês) “deve garantir que os fabricantes tenham medidas de segurança adequadas para evitar o uso indevido previsível e que os motoristas não sejam incentivados a depositar confiança perigosa em sistemas que ainda exigem toda a sua atenção.” Muitos motoristas de automóveis da Tesla afirmam que os sistemas lhes permitem tirar as mãos do volante por longos períodos, e alguns postaram vídeos sugerindo que podem realizar outras tarefas enquanto estão ao volante. A Tesla, o Departamento de Transportes (DOT, na sigla em inglês) e a NHTSA não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentário. “A NHTSA está ciente do crescente número de vídeos disponíveis publicamente que mostram motoristas da Tesla aparentemente dormindo ou de alguma forma desatentos à tarefa de dirigir enquanto o Autopilot ou o FSD estão em operação?”, questionou Krishnamoorthi. Ele quer saber se a NHTSA avaliou as medidas de segurança da Tesla para casos em que a câmera da cabine esteja obstruída, a visibilidade prejudicada ou quando os motoristas usem óculos escuros ou chapéus que interfiram na detecção. Em 2023, a Tesla fez um recall de cerca de 2 milhões de veículos -- quase todos os seus veículos elétricos nos EUA -- para garantir melhor que os motoristas prestem atenção ao usar o Autopilot. A Tesla afirmou que o Autopilot permite que os veículos dirijam, acelerem e freiem dentro de suas faixas, enquanto os veículos com Full Self-Driving podem obedecer aos sinais de trânsito e mudar de faixa. A montadora também afirmou que as duas tecnologias exigem motoristas “totalmente atentos” e com as mãos no volante. Em março, a NHTSA ampliou sua investigação sobre 3,2 milhões de veículos da Tesla equipados com o sistema de direção totalmente autônoma (FSD, na sigla em inglês), preocupada com a possibilidade de a tecnologia não conseguir detectar problemas ou alertar os motoristas em condições de baixa visibilidade. Em outubro, a NHTSA abriu uma investigação separada envolvendo 2,9 milhões de veículos Tesla equipados com o sistema FSD, devido a mais de 50 denúncias de violações de segurança no trânsito e uma série de acidentes. A agência de segurança veicular afirmou que o FSD -- um sistema de assistência que exige que os motoristas estejam atentos e intervenham se necessário -- “induziu um comportamento do veículo que violou as leis de segurança no trânsito”.

item.title: Infantino pode contar com votos suficientes para se manter na Fifa; adversários repensam estratégia, segundo fontes
item.description: O presidente da Fifa, Gianni Infantino, pode contar com votos suficientes para ser reeleito, o que significa que seus adversários precisarão mudar de estratégia e se concentrar em restringir seus poderes — uma reviravolta acentuada semanas depois que figuras importantes do futebol acreditavam que sua posição era insustentável, segundo informaram à Reuters várias fontes a par das discussões.
item.dc:creator: Julien Pretot
item.content:encoded: O presidente da Fifa, Gianni Infantino, pode contar com votos suficientes para ser reeleito, o que significa que seus adversários precisarão mudar de estratégia e se concentrar em restringir seus poderes — uma reviravolta acentuada semanas depois que figuras importantes do futebol acreditavam que sua posição era insustentável, segundo informaram à Reuters várias fontes a par das discussões. “Três semanas atrás, eu achava que ele estava acabado”, disse uma fonte do futebol mundial com conhecimento em primeira mão das discussões entre dirigentes sobre as chances de Infantino manter seu cargo. “O que eu não percebi foi até que ponto, após 10 anos no poder, as relações que ele construiu são quase inquebráveis.” Infantino, suíço-italiano de 56 anos, enfrentou o maior desafio à sua presidência este ano após o fracasso de sua proposta de vender uma participação de 20% nas competições da Fifa, incluindo a Copa do Mundo, a investidores privados. O plano gerou forte oposição, com a Uefa, a Confederação Asiática de Futebol e a Concacaf da América do Norte entre as entidades que clamavam por mudanças na liderança da Fifa. Várias federações nacionais europeias retiraram, desde então, o apoio à reeleição de Infantino, sendo a França a mais recente a fazê-lo nesta quinta-feira. Apesar de o secretário-geral da Fifa, Mattias Grafstrom, ter lamentado o que chamou de “série de eventos tristes e repreensíveis” que levou ao abandono do projeto, ele reafirmou posteriormente seu total apoio a Infantino após uma reunião de crise em Rabat. Mas, à medida que a crise imediata foi se dissipando, a aritmética eleitoral tornou-se cada vez mais desafiadora, afirmam os oponentes à reeleição de Infantino. Ainda não surgiu nenhum candidato capaz de angariar apoio suficiente entre as 211 federações membros da Fifa antes da eleição de março, enquanto Infantino mantém forte apoio entre nações com menor tradição no futebol e blocos importantes fora da Europa. No Congresso da Fifa, cada federação nacional terá um voto, o que significa que qualquer desafio bem-sucedido requer uma coalizão que vá muito além dos 55 membros da Uefa, órgão regulador europeu. Isso deixa os oponentes de Infantino diante de um cálculo potencialmente perigoso: desafiar o presidente e perder poderia fortalecer, em vez de enfraquecer, seu domínio sobre a Fifa. “Acho que o rumo mudou”, disse a fonte. “É um risco ainda maior para a Uefa ir à votação e não vencer.” Uefa e Fifa foram procuradas para comentar o assunto. AL-KHELAIFI DESISTE DA CANDIDATURA O presidente do Paris Saint-Germain, Nasser Al-Khelaifi, é considerado por figuras importantes do futebol como um dos poucos candidatos em potencial capazes de formar a coalizão interconfederacional necessária para derrotar Infantino. Fontes a par da situação acreditam que Al-Khelaifi poderia representar um desafio sério, mas ele se retirou da disputa, afirmando por meio de um porta-voz que não tem ambição, intenção ou interesse em se tornar presidente da Fifa. O presidente da Concacaf, Victor Montagliani, é outro nome que tem circulado, mas afirmou que provavelmente não se candidataria sem antes ter certeza de que conta com apoio suficiente para vencer, disse outra fonte do mundo do futebol à Reuters. Nenhum outro candidato de peso surgiu, embora um candidato africano ou asiático ainda possa ser indicado antes do prazo final de 18 de novembro, segundo a mesma fonte. Mesmo entre as confederações que continuam a apoiar Infantino, tem havido pedidos por uma governança mais forte, maior transparência e controles mais rígidos sobre as principais decisões comerciais da Fifa. Marrocos, uma das federações mais influentes da África, tem estado entre os apoiadores públicos de Infantino, que também mantém o apoio da Conmebol. Uma fonte sênior da Confederação Africana de Futebol disse à Reuters que algumas pessoas no meio do futebol africano acreditavam que o presidente da Real Federação Marroquina de Futebol, Fouzi Lekjaa, teria recebido a promessa de sediar a final da Copa do Mundo de 2030 em troca de ajudar a manter o apoio africano a Infantino. A Fifa negou as notícias de que Marrocos teria recebido a promessa da final em troca de apoio político. Lekjaa afirmou nesta quinta-feira que a final será realizada na região de Casablanca, embora a Fifa ainda não tenha anunciado formalmente o local. A federação marroquina não respondeu a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.

item.title: Spain issues permit to allow autonomous vehicle testing, Uber says
item.description: Spanish authorities have issued the first national permits to allow the testing of WeRide autonomous vehicles on public roads, Uber Technologies and WeRide said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spanish authorities have issued the first national permits to allow the testing of WeRide autonomous vehicles on public roads, Uber Technologies (UBER.N) and WeRide (WRD.O) said on Thursday. It said commercial services were planned by the end of the year in Madrid, subject to operational and regulatory milestones. Spain's Directorate-General for Traffic issued the permit and authorised preparation activities, including mapping, route validation and operational readiness testing, Uber said in a statement. It said the authorisation is the first national approval for WeRide's GXR vehicle in the European Union. The Madrid service would be WeRide and Uber's first joint autonomous vehicle deployment in Europe. Chinese company WeRide will provide autonomous driving technology and Uber will provide the ride-hailing app. AVOMO, the autonomous vehicle division of Spain's Moove Cars Group, will manage fleet operations, Uber said. WeRide and Uber plan to deploy tens of thousands of autonomous vehicles under a global partnership covering 15 cities by 2030. Earlier this month, Uber launched [USN:L8N44U25P TEXT:"autonomous rides in London"], making London its second European robotaxi market [USN:L4N44G1M1 TEXT:"after Zagreb"]. Spain's Directorate-General for Traffic did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside normal business hours.

item.title: Is Trump's $5,000 'dividend' legal and how would it work?
item.description: President Donald Trump on Wednesday proposed a $5,000 Trump dividend payment to U.S. adults if his Republicans retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Andy Sullivan, Jonathan Stempel, Saqib Ahmed
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump on Wednesday proposed a [USN:L1N45203G TEXT:"$5,000 "Trump dividend" payment"] to U.S. adults if his Republicans retain control of the House of Representatives and the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections . Here is what we know about Trump's pledge: WHO WOULD GET THE MONEY AND WHERE WOULD IT COME FROM? Trump said the checks would go to all adult U.S. citizens -- about 240 million people, according to the U.S. Census. That would cost a total of $1.2 trillion. Vice President JD Vance suggested on Fox News after Trump's speech that the U.S. government could draw on tariff revenue, which has been juiced by Trump's trade wars . The Congressional Budget Office estimates the government has taken in $167 billion so far in the fiscal year that ends September 30 -- not nearly enough to cover the cost of Trump's proposed giveaway. The payments would instead widen the government's budget gap, which is already at a level that [USN:S0N43F052 TEXT:"alarms budget watchdogs"]. CBO estimates the government will spend $2.1 trillion more than it collects in revenue in the current fiscal year and projects that figure will grow in the years to come as the population ages. WOULD THE PAYMENTS BE LEGAL? Candidates regularly promise benefits in return for votes. During the 2024 presidential campaign, Trump promised tax breaks for seniors, tipped workers and other targeted groups —and delivered them in his "One Big Beautiful Bill" the following year. Democratic candidates, including President-elect Joe Biden, promised a third round of COVID-19 relief checks in a Georgia special election in 2021 and delivered when they won control of Congress. The U.S. Supreme Court has ruled that a comparable promise is legal. In a unanimous 1982 decision, the high court overturned a lower-court ruling that had invalidated the election of a Kentucky official who had promised to save taxpayer money by lowering county commissioners' salaries. Elon Musk, the world's richest person, [USN:L6N42X16V TEXT:"offered voters a chance to win $1 million"] in 2024 if they signed a petition to support the Constitution. That drew legal challenges, still unresolved, from voters who said they had no real chance to win because Musk was seeking people to support his political action committee, which backed Republican candidates. It would be difficult to challenge Trump's dividend in court, as voters might have trouble showing that they had been directly harmed. WOULD THIS HAVE TO PASS CONGRESS? Yes. Congress has authority over spending under the U.S. Constitution. Trump's Republicans control both the House and the Senate by narrow margins, and several members of his party have already reacted favorably to the idea. Democrats would be sure to oppose any legislation and could block passage in the Senate, where a supermajority of 60 votes is needed to advance most legislation. Republicans could invoke a complex budget process to bypass Democrats and approve the bill along party lines. They have successfully used this approach twice since Trump's January 2025 return to office, but have struggled to advance a third such package. They have little time to act before the November 3 elections, as the House is scheduled to be in session for only one week before then. Congress could also try to act in a "lame-duck" session after the election. HAS THE U.S. GOVERNMENT GIVEN MONEY DIRECTLY TO CITIZENS BEFORE? Yes. Congress approved three separate direct payments in March 2020, December 2020 and March 2021 as part of sweeping relief packages to help people weather the economic disruption from the COVID-19 pandemic. Those payments — up to $1,200, $600 and $1,400 per adult, respectively — were phased out for higher-income people. That amounted to 476 million payments totaling $814 billion, according to a congressional oversight committee. Investigators found numerous logistical problems, including fraud and $1.4 billion sent to dead people. HOW WOULD THIS AFFECT THE ECONOMY AND FINANCIAL MARKETS? Economic studies have shown that the pandemic-era stimulus checks contributed to the subsequent rise in inflation by substantially boosting consumer demand. Those payments also boosted the stock market, with a measurable spike in retail trading volumes following each wave of stimulus deposits. But Trump's proposed dividend could upend bond markets if the government funded it through borrowing. The massive influx of new Treasury debt, combined with revived inflation fears, could drive bond prices sharply lower and send yields soaring. That could push government borrowing costs higher, further pressuring the U.S. budget at a time when interest payments already exceed military spending. Yields on [USN:L4N4520VC TEXT:"benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury bonds"] ticked up to 4.91% on Thursday as investors assessed Trump's proposal. HAS TRUMP MADE SIMILAR PROMISES IN THE PAST? Trump promised a similar $2,000 dividend in November 2025 tied to tariff revenue and said it would not apply to wealthy people, though no follow-up action was taken. Trump successfully sent a one-time "warrior dividend" payment of $1,776 to roughly 1.45 million military members in December 2025, drawing on money already approved by Congress. On Thursday, Trump's White House said nearly 1 million Americans will get [USN:FWN4520NI TEXT:"$500 payments"] to account for what it describes as excess fees charged for Affordable Care Act health insurance.

item.title: Ações fecham na mínima em dois meses após alta de juros pelo BCE alimentar apostas em novo aperto monetário
item.description: As ações europeias caíram para a mínima em dois meses nesta quinta-feira conforme aumentaram as expectativas de novas altas nas taxas de juros depois que o Banco Central Europeu elevou os custos dos empréstimos e alertou para um aumento da inflação devido ao choque de energia causado pela guerra.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: As ações europeias caíram para a mínima em dois meses nesta quinta-feira conforme aumentaram as expectativas de novas altas nas taxas de juros depois que o Banco Central Europeu elevou os custos dos empréstimos e alertou para um aumento da inflação devido ao choque de energia causado pela guerra. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) registrou queda de 0,7%, para 635,97 pontos, seu nível mais baixo desde 8 de julho. O BCE elevou nesta quinta-feira a taxa de depósito em 25 pontos-base, para 2,5%, segundo aumento neste ano, buscando garantir que o aumento nos preços da energia decorrente da guerra no Irã não se espalhe pela economia da zona do euro, que é particularmente vulnerável ao choque devido à sua dependência das importações de combustível. O banco central também aumentou sua projeção de crescimento econômico para 2026 de 0,8% para 0,9%, e agora espera uma inflação média de 3% neste ano. “Os riscos de inflação podem estar aumentando e um novo aumento em dezembro pode ser mais provável do que improvável, mas o BCE ainda precisa agir com cautela”, disse Mark Wall, economista-chefe para a Europa do Deutsche Bank. “A economia tem se mostrado resiliente nos últimos seis meses, mas o rápido aumento dos preços do gás significa que o choque negativo de oferta está se intensificando. Isso acabará prejudicando o crescimento.” A presidente do BCE, Christine Lagarde, afirmou em uma coletiva de imprensa após a reunião que “os riscos para as perspectivas de inflação são de alta” e que as pressões de preços podem permanecer acima da meta por um período prolongado. No entanto, ela ressaltou que o banco não se comprometeu antecipadamente com nenhuma medida futura. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) recuou 0,57%, a 10.608,92 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) caiu 0,84%, a 25.361,15 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) perdeu 0,49%, a 8.116,76 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve desvalorização de 0,13%, a 51.807,40 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou baixa de 0,18%, a 19.659,80 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) valorizou-se 0,11%, a 9.455,72 pontos.

item.title: Acciones europeas cierran en mínimo de dos meses, mercados apuestan a más alzas de tasas del BCE
item.description: Las acciones europeas cayeron el jueves a mínimos de dos meses, a medida que aumentan las expectativas de nuevas alzas de las tasas de interés después de que el Banco Central Europeo elevó los costos de financiación y advirtió de un repunte de la inflación debido a la crisis energética provocada por la guerra con Irán.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: Las acciones europeas cayeron el jueves a mínimos de dos meses, a medida que aumentan las expectativas de nuevas alzas de las tasas de interés después de que el Banco Central Europeo elevó los costos de financiación y advirtió de un repunte de la inflación debido a la crisis energética provocada por la guerra con Irán. * El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) perdió un 0,7%, a 635,97 puntos, su nivel más bajo desde el 8 de julio. La mayoría de los principales mercados regionales también cerraron en rojo. * El BCE elevó las tasas 25 puntos básicos, al 2,5%, su segundo alza del año. Las autoridades monetarias buscan garantizar que el aumento de los precios de la energía derivado de la guerra con Irán no se extienda a la economía de la zona euro, que es vulnerable a esta crisis por su dependencia de las importaciones de combustible. * La entidad también revisó del 0,8% previsto en junio al 0,9% su previsión de crecimiento económico para 2026, y ahora espera que la inflación se sitúe en un promedio del 3% este año. * La presidenta del BCE, Christine Lagarde, dijo en una rueda de prensa posterior a la reunión que "los riesgos para las perspectivas de inflación se inclinan al alza" y que las presiones sobre los precios podrían mantenerse por encima del objetivo durante un período prolongado. * El rendimiento de los bonos alemanes a 10 años, referencia para la zona del euro, tocó su máximo desde 2011. Los operadores esperan ahora una subida adicional de 60 puntos básicos en las tasas para la reunión de abril de 2027, frente a los cerca de 51 previos al anuncio. * Los precios del crudo se disparaban más de un 5% en la jornada, después de que el mayor repunte de ataques contra el transporte marítimo desde que comenzó la guerra con Irán avivó las preocupaciones de los operadores sobre posibles interrupciones en el suministro. * El sector minero (.SXPP) fue el más afectado, con una caída del 3,7%. Las mineras de cobre KGHM (KGH.WA) , Antofagasta (ANTO.L) , Aurubis (NAFG.DE) y Anglo American (AAL.L) perdieron entre un 5% y un 8%, ya que los precios del metal rojo bajaron después de que Reuters informó de que la Casa Blanca aún no ha tomado una decisión sobre los aranceles al cobre refinado.

item.title: Economia da França deve crescer apenas 0,4% este ano, afirma instituto de estatísticas
item.description: A economia da França crescerá menos este ano do que o governo havia previsto, já que a queda no poder de compra pesa sobre os gastos dos consumidores e as empresas restringem os investimentos, segundo a previsão divulgada nesta quinta-feira pelo Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INSEE), que revisou para baixo suas projeções.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A economia da França crescerá menos este ano do que o governo havia previsto, já que a queda no poder de compra pesa sobre os gastos dos consumidores e as empresas restringem os investimentos, segundo a previsão divulgada nesta quinta-feira pelo Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INSEE), que revisou para baixo suas projeções. A segunda maior economia da zona do euro deve agora crescer apenas 0,4% este ano, abaixo da previsão de 0,7% feita pelo INSEE em junho e menos da metade da expansão de 0,9% registrada no ano passado. Esse resultado ficaria aquém da previsão atual do governo de 0,7%, embora este deva revisar sua projeção na sexta-feira, enquanto se prepara para enviar seu projeto de lei orçamentária de 2027 ao Parlamento no final do mês. As perspectivas mais fracas tornam extremamente difícil atingir a meta atual de redução do déficit da França. O governo tinha como meta reduzir o déficit fiscal para 4,9% do Produto Interno Bruto este ano, ante 5,0% em 2025, mas também deve revisar essa previsão na sexta-feira. Em termos trimestrais, o INSEE prevê que o crescimento tenha apenas uma ligeira recuperação no segundo semestre do ano, após contração no primeiro e estagnação no segundo trimestre. Com as ondas de calor e a seca do verão afetando a produção agrícola, o crescimento foi estimado em apenas 0,1% no terceiro trimestre em relação aos três meses anteriores, antes de acelerar para 0,2% no último trimestre. (Reportagem de Leigh Thomas)

item.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs pleads no contest to misdemeanor charges
item.description: Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property on Thursday in a Green Bay (Wis.) courtroom.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Packers running back Josh Jacobs pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property on Thursday in a Green Bay (Wis.) courtroom. Jacobs was ordered to pay a $1,000 fine plus court costs on the battery charge, while the court deferred the proceedings on the criminal damage to property count for 12 months, at which time it will be dismissed upon completion of the terms of the agreement. A follow-up court date was set for Sept. 10, 2027. "I fully understand the seriousness of the situation and I take full responsibility," Jacobs said, per ESPN. Jacobs left the courthouse without speaking to the media. Thursday's court appearance was moved from November at Jacobs' request. He was charged with a pair of misdemeanors in connection to a May arrest just outside of Green Bay that local police referred to as a "disturbance complaint." Per multiple reports, the court ordered Jacobs to avoid contact with the alleged female victim, receive counseling, remain under supervision of criminal justice officials and pay restitution to the victim as part of accepting his plea. Jacobs, 28, was placed on the NFL commissioner's exempt list on Aug. 27. Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns in 15 games (all starts) last season. He also had 36 receptions for 282 yards and a score. Signed to a four-year, $48 million deal in 2024, Jacobs is a three-time Pro Bowl selection (2020, 2022, 2024). He also was a first-team All Pro in 2022, when he led the NFL in rushing yards with 1,653 yards as a member of the Las Vegas Raiders. Jacobs has rushed for 7,803 yards with 74 TDs in 105 games (104 starts) with the Raiders (2019-23) and Packers. He has 269 catches for 2,072 yards and two scores. The Raiders picked him in the first round (24th overall) in the 2019 NFL Draft out of Alabama. --Field Level Media

item.title: Leclerc y Hamilton aclaran la situación, pero no dejan normas de comportamiento por escrito
item.description: Charles Leclerc y su compañero de equipo en Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, afirmaron que habían aclarado las cosas cara a cara tras un encontronazo en el Gran Premio de Italia del pasado fin de semana, pero que aún no existían normas escritas de comportamiento entre ambos.
item.dc:creator: Alan Baldwin
item.content:encoded: Charles Leclerc y su compañero de equipo en Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, afirmaron que habían aclarado las cosas cara a cara tras un encontronazo en el Gran Premio de Italia del pasado fin de semana, pero que aún no existían normas escritas de comportamiento entre ambos. Hamilton, siete veces campeón del mundo de Fórmula Uno, había pedido unas normas por escrito después de que Leclerc le obligó a salirse a la grava en la primera vuelta y cayó del cuarto al décimo puesto. El británico acabó finalmente sexto, mientras que Leclerc sufrió un accidente y abandonó la carrera. Cuando se le preguntó el jueves, en el Gran Premio de España, si se había puesto algo por escrito, Hamilton respondió: "No, nada". "Estoy seguro de que, en algún momento, hablaremos de cómo podemos mejorar, pero no hemos tenido mucho tiempo para dar un giro a la situación. No se pueden cambiar las cosas en dos días", señaló. Hamilton afirmó que no hubo evasivas entre los dos pilotos a la hora de hablar de lo ocurrido. "Nos sentamos cara a cara, solo él y yo, y hablamos del tema", dijo. "Ambos fuimos abiertos y sinceros y zanjamos el asunto. Y podemos seguir adelante (...) Creo que es saludable. Es una relación que hemos construido con el tiempo". "Por supuesto que habrá frustraciones (…) Estoy seguro de que habrá más ocasiones en las que estemos muy cerca (en la pista), porque tenemos un ritmo muy similar. Los dos queremos ganar tanto como el otro y los dos queremos rendir bien para el equipo también", agregó. Ferrari ocupa el segundo puesto en el campeonato tras 13 pruebas, a 122 puntos de Mercedes. Hamilton es tercero en la clasificación general, a 76 puntos del líder, Kimi Antonelli de Mercedes. Leclerc dijo a la prensa que había revisado las imágenes tras la carrera y reconoció que se había pasado de la raya. "Se lo dije a Lewis y creo que está muy claro lo que debemos hacer o lo que debemos evitar de cara al futuro, pero no voy a entrar en más detalles sobre lo que hemos hablado", comentó el monegasco. "Lo único que puedo decir es que, sin duda, no ha afectado a la buena relación que tenemos y no afectará a nada de cara al futuro, y eso es lo más importante para mí, la verdad", indicó. Leclerc comentó que su accidente en Monza, al final de la segunda vuelta, le pareció grave y tuvo el cuello agarrotado durante un par de días después, pero que ahora ya se encuentra bien.

item.title: Nestle boosts cocoa buying in Brazil, working with farmers to cut fertilizer use
item.description: Global food and chocolate producer Nestle is increasing its cocoa sourcing in Brazil, where production is growing, and it is working with farmers on agricultural techniques that require less fertilizer, according to its CEO, Philipp Navratil.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Araujo
item.content:encoded: Global food and chocolate producer Nestle (NESN.S) is increasing its cocoa sourcing in Brazil, where production is growing, and it is working with farmers on agricultural techniques that require less fertilizer, according to its CEO, Philipp Navratil. Brazil was a major global supplier of cocoa in the 1970s, before a devastating fungus disease known as "Witch's Broom" decimated most plantations. [USN:L8N3OB1X0 TEXT:"Several large-scale farms"] have in recent years restarted production with more resilient trees, boosting the outlook for future production growth. Navratil told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday at Nestle's Caçapava plant, the world's largest producing unit for the popular KitKat chocolate candy, that the company has been working on improving its cocoa supply chain to make it more resilient following recent supply shocks that drove cocoa prices to all-time highs. "That means diversifying sourcing," he said. "Cocoa would be primarily sourced out of Western Africa. That was the number one source. And we have then decided Brazil is a really good place to go and look for high-quality cocoa," he said. Navratil said the company established relationships with hundreds of cocoa farms in Brazil to share technical information on regenerative agriculture, looking to increase quality and yields, as well as cutting the use of conventional fertilizers to reduce costs as farming input prices rose with the Middle East conflict. Cocoa trees, however, take up to five years to reach full production potential, so any significant change in the global supply chain will take time. Ecuador has been increasing cocoa fields for years and is now [USN:L2N3V909U TEXT:"approaching a similar volume to that of Ghana"], the world's second-largest supplier, with more than 600,000 metric tons of annual bean output. Ivory Coast leads production with around 2 million tons. Brazil still only produces enough for its domestic consumption, but the local government sees cocoa output doubling in five years to around 400,000 tons.

item.title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT for financial services industry
item.description: OpenAI on Thursday launched a version of ChatGPT built for the financial services industry, combining its latest AI model with built-in data from providers including LSEG , PitchBook and Daloopa to target investment bankers and equity researchers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: OpenAI on Thursday launched a version of ChatGPT built for the financial services industry, combining its latest AI model with built-in data from providers including LSEG (LSEG.L) , PitchBook and Daloopa to target investment bankers and equity researchers. The product, ChatGPT for Financial Services, was developed with Morgan Stanley (MS.N) and Evercore (EVR.N) as design partners to help shape the offering, OpenAI said in a blog post. The launch reflects a broader push by AI companies to build products for regulated industries where data governance and security are central concerns. The product builds on ChatGPT Enterprise's existing security controls, including role-based access and encryption, and allows compliance teams to export workspace logs into audit workflows. The service is powered by GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's newest model, which the company said was built to improve retrieval across financial data tools, financial reasoning and the accuracy of generated content. Users can conduct research across multiple sources, build financial models and generate client materials such as pitchbooks using their firm's own templates, OpenAI said. OpenAI said it plans to expand the breadth of financial data available through the product and further train its models to identify, interpret and apply that information across tasks traditionally handled by experienced analysts. The product includes datasets from Daloopa, LSEG News, PitchBook, Crunchbase, Quartr and others covering earnings transcripts, financial statements and company fundamentals. OpenAI said the data is indexed on its own infrastructure to improve retrieval and citation. LSEG serves as the sole distributor of Reuters news, financial data, and real-time alerts to global financial professionals. Firms that already hold data subscriptions can connect them through integrations with FactSet (FDS.N) , S&P Global, Preqin and Datasite, the company said. OpenAI said it plans to expand the product beyond investment banking and equity research across the wider financial services sector.

item.title: Woad set for Korda showdown on Solheim Cup debut
item.description: England's Lottie Woad will make her eagerly awaited Solheim Cup debut alongside Charley Hull against unbeaten American duo Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz in Friday's foursomes at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England's Lottie Woad will make her eagerly awaited Solheim Cup debut alongside Charley Hull against unbeaten American duo Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz in Friday's foursomes at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands. Europe are seeking to reclaim the team trophy after the U.S. won in Virginia in 2024. The 22-year-old Woad faces a tough start against world number one Korda, who has won all four of her foursomes matches alongside Corpuz in the last two editions. But Woad, one of four rookies in Anna Nordqvist's team, will be able to count on the experience of Hull, who is making her eighth successive appearance. Friday's other foursomes will see Europe's Nanna Koerstz Madsen and Celine Boutier take on Alison Lee and Lauren Coughlin, Esther Henseleit and Leona Maguire against Andrea Lee and Lindy Duncan and Maja Stark and Linn Grant playing Rose Zhang and Jennifer Kupcho. "Charley and Lottie, they've got to play (together) quite a bit on tour this year, so I think they were both very excited to be paired with each other," Nordqvist said after the draw. "If you are going to be anywhere (on Friday) you want to be on the first tee because it doesn't get better than that." U.S. captain Angela Stanford said pairing Korda and Corpuz was her easiest selection decision. "If I didn't put those two out (Korda and Corpuz), I would be questioned. I feel like the whole world knew that they were coming," she said on Thursday. "We can talk about Nelly and we can talk about her being the number one player in the world, but don't sleep on Allisen. I've called her the backbone of our team." The U.S. are trying to retain the trophy and claim a first victory on European soil since 2015. The last three editions in Europe have all been titanic tussles with no more than one point separating the sides who are tied on 42 points apiece from those matches. Three years ago in Andalusia the U.S. team led 4-0 after Friday foursomes, but Europe hit back to clinch a thrilling 14-14 tie after Sunday's singles to retain the trophy. "Even if you're a couple down early, you can get it back and even just getting a half point could be vital," Woad said as she looked ahead to her debut. "So I think you've just got to have that mentality that any half point or point helps."

item.title: DVF returns to runway spotlight with Henry Zankov at the helm
item.description: Guests in wrap dresses and bright colors gathered on New York's High Line on Thursday as Belgian fashion designer Diane von Furstenberg returned to the runway for the first time in nearly a decade, opening New York Fashion Week.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Broadway, Jenna Zucker
item.content:encoded: Guests in wrap dresses and bright colors gathered on New York's High Line on Thursday as Belgian fashion designer Diane von Furstenberg returned to the runway for the first time in nearly a decade, opening New York Fashion Week. New artistic director Henry Zankov made his debut for the label, marking a homecoming. Zankov joined DVF as a knitwear designer in 2014, spent four years at the company and later launched his own namesake brand. Zankov told Reuters he aims to carry forward von Furstenberg’s legacy through "body language and sensuality and seduction and fabric and freedom." While the house’s signature wrap dress remained central to the collection, appearing alongside wrap tops and flowing capes, Zankov pushed a bolder mix of prints, textures and color. Animal prints met vivid blocks of color and clashing patterns, while metallic pieces added flashes of shine. The collection reflected Zankov’s view of modern womanhood as something that transcends age. "I think all women are modern. The clothes are like tools and you use them how you want to," he said. The show returned DVF to the New York Fashion Week calendar while placing Zankov, known for his colorful, graphic knitwear, at the helm of one of American fashion’s most recognizable brands. Von Furstenberg founded DVF in 1972, whose mission is to empower women through style.

item.title: Peru to join US anti-drug coalition after Rubio visit
item.description: Peru will join the U.S.-led "Shield of the Americas" coalition against drug cartels, President Keiko Fujimori said on Thursday after talks with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Lima, tightening security ties with Washington early in her presidency.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Peru will join the U.S.-led "Shield of the Americas" coalition against drug cartels, President [USN:L6N43Q0ZQ TEXT:"Keiko Fujimori"] said on Thursday after talks with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Lima, tightening security ties with Washington early in her presidency. Peru's [USN:S0N42A02L TEXT:"foreign ministry"] had flagged the move in recent months as part of a broader push to strengthen border security and coordination against transnational crime. Fujimori told reporters Peru's participation in the coalition would help speed intelligence-sharing and bolster joint action against criminal groups operating across borders. Rubio, welcoming the decision, said the initiative was meant to "shield the region" from organizations that threaten the sovereignty of countries across the hemisphere, according to remarks delivered at the joint appearance. Rubio's visit, the highest-level U.S. trip to Peru since President Donald Trump returned to office, comes as Washington seeks closer security and commercial ties with conservative governments in Latin America while pushing back against China's influence in mining and infrastructure. Peru is the world's third-largest copper producer, giving the relationship added strategic weight for both governments. The two countries have already moved to deepen defense ties. In January, the United States designated Peru a major non-NATO ally, and the State Department approved a possible $1.5 billion foreign military sale for design and construction work at Callao naval base, Peru's main naval hub near Lima. The Peru stop capped Rubio's three-country South America tour this week, after visits to Colombia and Ecuador, centered on counternarcotics, migration and trade. In Lima, officials also discussed U.S. support for Peru's preparations for a possible El Niño emergency, Fujimori said.

item.title: In-house counsel group accuses rival of training AI on its materials
item.description: The Association of Corporate Counsel, a nonprofit bar association for in-house attorneys, sued competitor The L Suite in Delaware federal court on Thursday for allegedly copying its materials to train a lawyer-focused chatbot.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: The Association of Corporate Counsel, a nonprofit bar association for in-house attorneys, sued competitor The L Suite in Delaware federal court on Thursday for allegedly copying its materials to train a lawyer-focused chatbot. The lawsuit said that The L Suite trained its chatbot Lloyd on copyrighted works including at least one ACC report, and that it "brazenly" promoted Lloyd with an image of the report and an ACC trademark. Spokespeople for The L Suite did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the complaint. "We made a good-faith effort to resolve this matter directly, and when that effort failed, filing this complaint became necessary to protect our members’ interests and the integrity of ACC’s work," ACC president Jason Brown said in a statement. The Washington-based ACC has more than 48,000 members and publishes content, including continuing legal education materials, surveys and white papers. The L Suite, which calls itself "the leading general counsel community on its website," announced the launch of its Lloyd chatbot in May. The L Suite said in a press release that Lloyd "combines foundational AI capabilities with the trusted judgment of thousands of accomplished in-house legal executives." The ACC said in its complaint that an L Suite video promoting Lloyd displayed the cover of an ACC report. "As a result, there can be no doubt that The L Suite was specifically aware that its Lloyd platform was utilizing ACC materials," the lawsuit said. The ACC also alleged that The L Suite violated its trademark rights in the phrase "By In-House Counsel, For In-House Counsel" by using "Built By In-House Counsel, For In-House Counsel" in its Lloyd advertising. The ACC requested monetary damages and a court order blocking The L Suite from using its trademarks and copyrighted materials. The case is Association of Corporate Counsel v. The L Suite Inc, U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, No. 1:26-cv-01138. For the ACC: Robert Leighton and Paul Sauerteig of Goldberg Kohn For The L Suite: attorney information not yet available

item.title: El plan de la Casa Blanca de aranceles al cobre se frena ante preocupación por economía: fuentes
item.description: La Casa Blanca aún no ha tomado una decisión sobre los aranceles al cobre refinado, ya que los responsables están considerando la preocupación de que el aumento de los precios del metal pueda subir los costos de fabricación frente a las ventajas de fomentar una mayor actividad minera nacional, según dos personas familiarizadas con el asunto.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw, Ernest Scheyder
item.content:encoded: La Casa Blanca aún no ha tomado una decisión sobre los aranceles al cobre refinado, ya que los responsables están considerando la preocupación de que el aumento de los precios del metal pueda subir los costos de fabricación frente a las ventajas de fomentar una mayor actividad minera nacional, según dos personas familiarizadas con el asunto. El Gobierno se está centrando cada vez más en los precios antes de las elecciones legislativas de noviembre, y tanto el presidente Donald Trump como los legisladores republicanos se ven presionados para demostrar que sus políticas económicas están reduciendo —en lugar de aumentar— los costos para los consumidores y las empresas estadounidenses. Los precios del cobre se han disparado a máximos históricos por las expectativas de que Trump impondrá aranceles a los productos de cobre refinado, como los cátodos, así como al concentrado de cobre producido en las minas. Los operadores y los compradores industriales se han apresurado a acumular existencias en Estados Unidos para adelantarse a cualquier nuevo arancel, creando así una de las mayores reservas de cobre del mundo. Un funcionario de la Casa Blanca dijo que la Administración no había tomado una decisión definitiva sobre los aranceles y confirmó que el Departamento de Comercio había facilitado información actualizada a Trump antes de la fecha límite del 30 de junio fijada por la Casa Blanca. "La Administración sigue evaluando todas las opciones para repatriar la producción de cobre y otros sectores manufactureros críticos a Estados Unidos", dijo el funcionario. Las declaraciones sugieren que los aranceles no son un hecho consumado, a pesar de que el mercado espera que Estados Unidos pueda subir los existentes al cobre refinado. La Administración ha estado barajando la posibilidad de aplicar aranceles al cobre refinado como parte de la iniciativa más amplia de Trump para revivir la industria manufacturera estadounidense y reducir la dependencia de los suministros extranjeros de materiales críticos. Las acciones de los productores de cobre caían tras la noticia de Reuters. Las de Freeport (FCX.N) bajaban un 7% en la sesión bursátil del jueves al mediodía, las de Rio (RIO.L) perdían un 2,7% y las de BHP (BHP.AX) retrocedían un 4,7%. Los precios del cobre perdieron más del 4%. El cobre se usa en la construcción, el transporte, la electrónica y muchos otros sectores. S&P Global (SPGI.N) prevé que el crecimiento en los sectores de la inteligencia artificial y la defensa impulse la demanda mundial de cobre un 50% para 2040. Estados Unidos importa aproximadamente la mitad de sus necesidades de cobre cada año y solo cuenta con dos fundiciones de cobre actibas, propiedad de Freeport-McMoRan y Rio Tinto, respectivamente. Los aranceles propuestos podrían encarecer el cobre importado y mejorar la rentabilidad de los proyectos mineros, de fundición y de refinación de Estados Unidos. Sin embargo, unos aranceles más amplios sobre el cobre también podrían aumentar los costos para los fabricantes que dependen de este metal, incluidos los productores de equipos eléctricos, automóviles, materiales de construcción y otros bienes industriales. La tensión ha complicado los esfuerzos de la Administración por usar los aranceles para fomentar la producción nacional sin agravar la inflación ni socavar el mensaje político de Trump sobre la reducción del costo de la vida. La incertidumbre arancelaria también está impidiendo que el cobre llegue a mercados fuera de Estados Unidos, lo que restringe aún más la oferta mundial. "Mientras la política (arancelaria) siga sin resolverse, esa posibilidad reduce el incentivo para devolver el metal a los mercados internacionales", dijo Jacob White, analista de minerales de Sprott Asset Management, que invierte en productores de cobre.

item.title: Madring gives F1 a blind date with 'Monumental' mayhem
item.description: Formula One rolls into Madrid this weekend for a first look at the Madring, a new Spanish Grand Prix venue with a banked beast of a corner and enough unknowns to have drivers reaching for the word of the day: challenging.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: Formula One rolls into Madrid this weekend for a first look at the Madring, a new Spanish Grand Prix venue with a banked beast of a corner and enough unknowns to have drivers reaching for the word of the day: challenging. Spain is hosting two races this season, with Madrid's street circuit around the IFEMA exhibition centre following Barcelona's Catalunya Grand Prix on the calendar. The Madring is the first new circuit since Las Vegas three years ago and brings down the curtain on the regular European leg of the season. The Madring's signature flourish comes at Turn 12, where [USN:L6N4500ZT TEXT:""La Monumental""] slings the cars around a long, banked arc before spitting them over a crest, leaving drivers momentarily aiming at grandstands built to hold up to 45,000 fans — and the blue sky — rather than tarmac. Until now, most of the field have only met the circuit in the simulator, leaving teams to untangle set-ups and racing lines on a layout whose pecking order remains guesswork. "It looks different. It looks that the track has character, that is charismatic, with a lot of different kinds of corners," Madrid-born Williams driver Carlos Sainz, an ambassador for the track, told a press conference on Thursday. "At least we can take that away, that that is going to be a different track to what we're used to." Sainz has driven a few laps in a road car on an unfinished version of the track, but said that was "nowhere as representative as the laps that I did in the simulator". Ferrari pair Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton are the only other drivers with some prior experience of the Madring after driving there during a filming day in July, when the circuit was still more building site than Grand Prix theatre. Hamilton, the seven-times world champion, was quick to pour cold water on any suggestion of an advantage. "I think it's hardly any," he told reporters. "It was dusty, super, super dusty. There was zero grip. We couldn't change the car because it's not a test. It was filming. "We weren't even flat out in many of the corners. We were low, just low power, low grip. The benefit, the only one thing is I've seen which way the track goes. So honestly, I don't think we have any advantage." SWEEPING SPECTACLE The circuit is built partly inside Madrid's convention centre and partly on the streets of Valdebebas, across from soccer side Real Madrid's training ground. Its mix of enclosed sections, tight walls and sweeping spectacle has intrigued drivers, though overtaking may be at a premium. La Monumental, with its diagonal banking and vast grandstand backdrop, carries echoes of American oval racing and has the potential to feel more like a stadium than a conventional circuit. Hamilton said the layout reminded him partly of Montreal's kerbs, but compared the difficulty of learning it to Saudi Arabia's Jeddah circuit, introduced in 2021. "It's a massively challenging circuit," he said. "Of all the new tracks that I've gone to, this one, maybe Saudi, I like the two closest in terms of how difficult it was to get on top of the car and find the right lines." Leclerc also expects qualifying to take on extra weight. "It looked like a very challenging track, and I think exactly the kind of track that I enjoy as a driver," he told reporters. "It's true to say as well that I think coming Sunday the amount of overtaking opportunities there will be will be very little, but I think in qualifying it will be a very cool and challenging track for all drivers." That could make Saturday the weekend's main act. "I think it's the kind of weekend where you want to focus more on the qualifying pace than on the race pace," Leclerc said. "The priority will be shifted a little bit more towards qualifying."

item.title: Jamaican sprint star Bolt marvels at prize money on eve of inaugural Ultimate Championship
item.description: Had the World Athletics Ultimate Championship existed in his prime, Usain Bolt says he would have been first in line to compete, drawn not only by the chance to race the world's best but also by the richest prize pot in the sport's history.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Had the World Athletics Ultimate Championship existed in his prime, Usain Bolt says he would have been first in line to compete, drawn not only by the chance to race the world's best but also by the richest prize pot in the sport's history. "I was having a conversation with Asafa (former world record-holder Powell). We were actually talking about that same thing," Bolt said on Thursday. "We're like, 'jeez, we missed out with this cash prize.'" Winners of individual events pocket $150,000, while the winning relay teams share $80,000, meaning a sprinter contesting the 100, 200 and mixed 4x100 metres relay could leave Budapest with a tidy sum. "I won a few championships, and it still doesn't add up to all the cash, so it's big," said Bolt, the 100m and 200m world record-holder. "It's good for the sport, it incentivises athletes to do their best. Sorry I missed out on it." Bolt's comments strike at the heart of World Athletics' latest experiment. Seeking to attract younger audiences and keep pace in an increasingly crowded sports market, the governing body has launched the event as a high-stakes showcase built around elite head-to-head competition, big prize money and a faster, more engaging presentation. "We're really spotlighting the stars and creating new formats," World Athletics President Sebastian Coe said. STREAMLINED SCHEDULE The governing body has introduced a streamlined schedule designed to eliminate downtime, along with innovations including a black infield with theatrical lighting. "We want this championship to be an incubator for change," Coe said. "It's an event that has been created with and by the fans, with and by the athletes." Organisers also rolled out a red-carpet event on Thursday to put athletes front and centre, part of a broader effort to showcase personalities beyond performances and help fans connect with the sport's stars. Reigning Olympic 100m champion Noah Lyles wore a rhinestoned black velvet Yves Saint Laurent suit, while pole vault world record-holder Mondo Duplantis, who also wrote and performed the event's anthem entitled "Gold," went for a more understated blue suit and shades. "You don't want to miss it. Something big could always happen when I step out on the track or anybody," said Duplantis. "It's going to be athletics displayed in a way that's never been seen before." One question hanging over the competition has been whether athletes need another major meet in a year that would traditionally have been free of a world championships or Olympic Games. "If you follow my career, you know that's what I'm about -- competing against the best," Bolt said. "With the Ultimate Championship, you know that 16 people who show up are the best in the world, I would look at it as big as the Olympics and the World Championships for sure." For 2008 Olympic 100m hurdles champion Dawn Harper-Nelson, who is a celebrity broadcaster for the event, the stakes extend beyond prize money and presentation. "It's bringing the attention to the sport that we begged for," she said. "You asked for it, and now the time has come."

item.title: Grupo português D3 processa Meta, TikTok e YouTube por design viciante
item.description: O grupo português de direitos digitais D3 entrou com ações judiciais contra Facebook , Instagram, TikTok e YouTube , acusando-os de criarem recursos em suas plataformas que mantêm os usuários viciados, informou o grupo nesta quinta-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O grupo português de direitos digitais D3 entrou com ações judiciais contra Facebook (META.O) , Instagram, TikTok e YouTube (GOOGL.O) , acusando-os de criarem recursos em suas plataformas que mantêm os usuários viciados, informou o grupo nesta quinta-feira. As quatro ações coletivas, que permitem que associações apresentem casos em nome de um grupo mais amplo de consumidores, são um desdobramento de processos judiciais em outros países que contestaram o design viciante das mídias sociais. Nenhuma das empresas proprietárias das plataformas processadas — Meta, ByteDance e Alphabet — respondeu imediatamente aos pedidos de comentários da Reuters. A ação judicial, apresentada pelo escritório de advocacia Andersen Tax & Legal Iberia no Tribunal Cível de Lisboa entre abril e maio e divulgada somente agora após o recesso judicial de verão, busca "responsabilizar essas plataformas e obrigá-las a proporcionar uma experiência segura para seus usuários", afirmou a D3. A D3 destacou recursos como rolagem infinita, vídeos com reprodução automática, notificações persistentes e sistemas de recomendação altamente personalizados, presentes no Facebook e Instagram da Meta, no TikTok da ByteDance e no YouTube da Alphabet. Ao eliminar as pausas naturais no uso, fornecer conteúdo personalizado constantemente e incentivar repetidamente os usuários a retornar, as plataformas criam ciclos de feedback comportamental semelhantes às técnicas usadas há muito tempo na indústria de jogos de azar, disse a D3. "As plataformas não precisam ser hiperviciantes", disse Ricardo Lafuente, presidente da D3. "Um ecossistema de mídia social saudável, produtivo e educativo é possível, mas somente se as regras forem robustas, aplicadas corretamente e direcionadas àqueles que persistem em ignorá-las", disse ele. Em ambos os lados do Atlântico, as mídias sociais têm sido alvo de crescente escrutínio. Em fevereiro, o TikTok foi acusado, de acordo com as normas da UE, por supostos recursos viciantes, enquanto em agosto a meta concordou em pagar até US$18 bilhões para encerrar processos judiciais nos EUA relacionados ao vício. Segundo dados compilados pelo site SocialMediaTransparency.org, as quatro plataformas alcançaram um total de 33 milhões de usuários mensais em Portugal no primeiro semestre de 2026. (Por Sergio Gonçalves)

item.title: Julia Donaldson and Axel Scheffler reflect on a lifetime of storytelling as they reveal new Gruffalo book
item.description: As the latest instalment in the Gruffalo series reached bookshelves on Thursday, author Julia Donaldson and illustrator Axel Scheffler reflected on more than two decades of collaboration, saying the enduring popularity of their beloved monster had exceeded anything they imagined when they first created him.
item.dc:creator: Francesca Halliwell
item.content:encoded: As the latest instalment in the Gruffalo series reached bookshelves on Thursday, author Julia Donaldson and illustrator Axel Scheffler reflected on more than two decades of collaboration, saying the enduring popularity of their beloved monster had exceeded anything they imagined when they first created him. Donaldson, whose Gruffalo books have sold more than 18.2 million copies worldwide, said she tries not to dwell on how many children listen to her stories at bedtime, joking that the thought would keep her awake at night. "Gruffalo Granny", the first new Gruffalo story in more than 20 years, follows the Gruffalo and his daughter as they prepare for a visit from her Granny, whose huge appetite sends them in search of a meal. The mouse they capture plots its escape, while they plan to serve it for dinner. Speaking at the book's launch in London, Donaldson said the idea may have been influenced by her own family life. "I've got nine grandchildren, and in this story, it ends up with the grandmother telling stories to the grandchild, so maybe that was at the back of my mind," she said. Scheffler, who has illustrated several Donaldson books including "Room on the Broom" and "Stick Man", said he had never expected there would be another Gruffalo sequel, despite the original book having been translated into 113 languages and dialects. The pair said their decades-long partnership has thrived because they work largely independently, joking that limited contact during the creative process may be the secret to their success. As to whether they might make another sequel in future, Donaldson and Scheffler suggested clumsy dragon "Zog" could be a candidate for another outing, despite having already spawned one follow-up story. With a National Literacy Trust report published earlier this year finding that just over one in three children in the UK enjoys reading in their spare time, Scheffler said he hopes their books encourage children to read and be creative. Donaldson said she is heartened by letters from young readers who write stories of their own and remains optimistic about the future of books. "I started writing because of the books and poems that I read as a child, so it's nice to think of it as a kind of chain going through the generations," she said. "I love reading. I think it's one of the greatest pleasures there is, so I just feel it will last."

item.title: Cutting Canada tariffs alone won't flatten US aluminum premium, Alcoa says
item.description: The steep premium paid for aluminum in the U.S. will not drop significantly even if Washington halves the tariffs on metal from neighboring Canada, because imports from other countries will still be needed, Alcoa's finance chief said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The steep premium paid for aluminum in the U.S. will not drop significantly even if Washington halves the tariffs on metal from neighboring Canada, because imports from other countries will still be needed, Alcoa's (AA.N) finance chief said on Thursday. The price U.S. consumers pay on top of the London Metal Exchange benchmark for physical aluminum, known as the Midwest premium , is high at $1.09 per lb, or $2,403 per metric ton, but has eased from a record $1.19 in June on hopes the 50% import tariff [USN:S0N40K03S TEXT:"could be halved"] for Canadian material. Speaking at the Jefferies Global Industrials Conference in New York, Alcoa Chief Financial Officer Molly Beerman noted that the U.S. needed to import around 4 million tons of aluminum per year and Canada could only supply 3 million tons of that. "With the U.S. still needing to incent the import of a million tons, even if we were to have a favorable rate with Canada, we don't see Midwest dropping significantly," Beerman said. "It might come off a little bit, but we wouldn't see it returning to pre-tariff levels." If there is tariff relief or waivers for other trade partners -- such as Japan, South Korea or Europe -- and the last 1 million tons is covered, "then you can expect the Midwest premium to reduce in response to essentially wipe out the tariff benefit," Beerman said. Pittsburgh-based Alcoa produces around 900,000 tons per year of aluminum in Canada and is paying more than $1 billion in tariffs to bring most of it into the U.S., Beerman said. "However, the Midwest is fully compensating us for that, as well as returning as margin because of the tightness in tons." With aluminum supplies from the war-hit Middle East constrained, customers in North America and Europe are "actively looking for our supply," Beerman said, noting that Alcoa's order book was "almost completely sold out for the rest of 2026."

item.title: Fake Fox News graphic says Trump ordered death penalty for Lindsay Clancy
item.description: A fabricated Fox News graphic was shared online to claim that U.S. President Donald Trump has imposed the death penalty on Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother whose trial for killing her three young children ended in a mistrial on September 4.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A fabricated Fox News graphic was shared online to claim that U.S. President Donald Trump has imposed the death penalty on Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother whose trial for killing her three young children [USN:L1N44V0ZD TEXT:"ended in a mistrial"] on September 4. Here are the key details: Clancy’s attorneys argued that she was not guilty by reason of insanity because the tragedy occurred while she was suffering from postpartum psychosis. A September 3 X post shared the fabricated graphic featuring Fox News’ logo with the text: “President Trump Issues Executive Order To Throw Down the Death Penalty On Lindsay Clancy.” However, a spokesperson for the outlet told Reuters that it was not an authentic Fox News graphic. There are no credible reports of such an order from Trump, who has said publicly that he had been following the trial and that Clancy’s [USN:L1N4500KR TEXT:"lawyer had asked"] Trump to pardon her, even though the case was prosecuted under state law. Massachusetts law does not authorize capital punishment under its current murder statute. A White House spokesperson said by email, "this is obviously fake." Trump signed an executive order on January 20, 2025, directing the U.S. Department of Justice to pursue the federal death penalty in eligible federal cases. He has not imposed the order on a specific defendant in any case. Verdict: False. The image does not show an authentic Fox News graphic and there are no credible reports of Trump imposing or calling for the death penalty for Lindsay Clancy. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

item.title: Robinson strikes twice as England close in on Pakistan whitewash
item.description: Ollie Robinson continued his outstanding summer with two wickets in his opening over as England pushed Pakistan towards defeat in the third test at Edgbaston on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Neil Squires
item.content:encoded: Ollie Robinson continued his outstanding summer with two wickets in his opening over as England pushed Pakistan towards defeat in the third test at Edgbaston on Thursday. Robinson, man of the match in the first two tests, struck with the first ball of Pakistan’s second innings and again three deliveries later to leave England closing in on a 3-0 series whitewash. The demoralised tourists reached 52-2 before rain ended play early on day two, needing 268 runs to make England bat again. Robinson, 32, has been almost unplayable in this series, taking 21 wickets at an average of under seven runs each. He continued in the same vein in Birmingham, removing Saim Ayub, who was dismissed for a duck in both innings, and then Abdullah Shafique to finish the day with figures of 2-10 from his six overs. "He’s probably one of the most consistent bowlers in world cricket. He knows what he’s doing with the ball and he wears you down a bit so it’s a challenge,” said Pakistan batting coach Mike Smith. "He has bowled exceptionally well and he’s in a little purple patch as a player. We need to find a way to combat that as well as we can." Shan Masood, who was dropped at slip by Ben Duckett off Gus Atkinson, was still there on 21 at the close, alongside opener Azan Awais on 29, but Pakistan's position appears hopeless. England, who led by 23 overnight, had earlier pressed the accelerator to extend their first-innings advantage to a daunting 320. They made 453 with Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence extending their fifth-wicket partnership to 86 until Brook set off for an impossible single and was run out by Masood for 75 from 97 balls. Lawrence went on to make 65 from 82 balls before dragging a wide ball onto his stumps to give Mohammad Imran his first test wicket. It was a third test half-century in a row for Lawrence, who was recalled after a two-year absence for this series. "I'm really happy with how I've contributed," said Lawrence. "I was feeling really good today, got on a bit of a roll with Brooky and went with it. "I thought I was going to make a really big score to be honest. It wasn’t to be but I think if I’d been offered 65 at the start of the day I’d have taken it." There was also a welcome half-century from the out-of-form Jamie Smith, who overcame an uncertain start and a finger injury, which caused him to hand over the wicketkeeping gloves to Jordan Cox, to strike 69 off 84 balls including one six and nine fours. It was his highest test score since a second-innings 88 against India on the same ground 14 months ago. Robinson chimed in with a 50 of his own, which included a huge six into the Hollies Stand off Mohammad Abbas, before becoming Razaullah’s fourth victim. The blooding of the 21-year-old, who had only played eight first-class games prior to his call-up, was one of the few positives for Pakistan. While he was expensive – he conceded 148 runs off his 23 overs – he posed a threat with his pace and aggression. Razaullah may represent a brighter future for Pakistan, but the present remains bleak for a team that has lost 15 of its last 20 tests.

item.title: US appeals court rejects Trump mail-in ballot restrictions as Supreme Court considers rule
item.description: A U.S. appeals court on Thursday declined to allow President Donald Trump's administration to implement a new U.S. Postal Service rule that would tighten mail-in voting requirements before November's congressional elections, as the U.S. Supreme Court weighs a similar request.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A U.S. appeals court on Thursday declined to allow President Donald Trump's administration to implement a new U.S. Postal Service rule that would tighten mail-in voting requirements before November's congressional elections, as the U.S. Supreme Court weighs a similar request. A three-judge panel of the Boston-based 1st U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals declined to put on hold an injunction that a lower-court judge issued last week that has prevented USPS from enforcing the new rule it adopted at the Republican president's direction. The fate of that rule will be decided soon by the 6-3 conservative-majority U.S. Supreme Court.
